Communication by telephone and telegram is common but slow and monitored
Physical restraint and hostage-taking possible but must be covert and plausible

surface_summary: Stanley Rees, a young director of the British and Imperial Granaries, mysteriously disappears. The company directors, including Phipps and Dredlinton, face public outrage over their wheat speculation. Wingate, an American financier and enemy of Phipps, threatens and confronts the directors amid rising tensions.
accepted_facts: Stanley Rees has disappeared from his hotel room without explanation
The British and Imperial Granaries have cornered a large portion of the wheat market
Wingate is an enemy of Phipps and opposes the company's speculation
The directors have been under pressure and receiving threatening letters
inferred_conclusions: Stanley Rees disappeared voluntarily to escape scandal
Wingate is innocent and only a concerned friend
The disappearance is unrelated to the wheat speculation
mechanism_description: John Wingate orchestrates the kidnapping of the three directors—Phipps, Dredlinton, and Rees—holding them hostage in Dredlinton's house. He uses this to blackmail them into selling wheat at a drastically reduced price to break their market corner. The captivity is maintained by trusted servants and accomplices, ensuring secrecy and control.
delivery_path: Stanley Rees is lured from his hotel and brought secretly to Dredlinton House
Phipps is similarly brought to the house under false pretenses
Dredlinton is subdued and confined in his own home
Wingate controls the servants and communications to isolate the captives
The captives are bound and gagged, then released only after agreeing to sell wheat
Dredlinton dies from exhaustion during captivity
The captives are released after the sale is confirmed
outcome_result: The directors are forced to sell wheat at a lower price, breaking their corner, and the kidnapped men are released, though Dredlinton dies during captivity.

false_assumption.statement: Stanley Rees disappeared voluntarily to avoid scandal or personal trouble.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: Rees was seen leaving his room without coat or hat and had social engagements that evening, suggesting a voluntary absence. The lack of immediate evidence of foul play supports this.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: It conceals the fact that Rees was abducted and held hostage as part of a calculated scheme to force the directors to break their wheat corner.

supporting_points: Wingate is the enemy of the directors and openly threatens them
He is present at many key moments and has access to the house
He shows knowledge of the disappearance and market manipulation
He controls the servants and communications
false_solution.the_one_flaw: Wingate orchestrates the kidnapping but is not the victimizer; the actual blackmail and market manipulation are carried out by the directors themselves under duress.

red_herrings.description: Lord Dredlinton's drunken outbursts and aggressive behavior suggest he might be responsible for Rees' disappearance.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: His drunkenness is genuine but he is himself a victim of the kidnapping and blackmail scheme.

red_herrings.description: Peter Phipps' ruthless market dealings and threats imply he might have orchestrated the disappearance to protect his interests.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Though involved in the scheme, Phipps is coerced and held hostage, not the mastermind.

closed_circle.rationale: The disappearance and hostage situation involve only the directors and Wingate, all confined within Dredlinton House with no outside access, forming a closed circle of suspects and victims.

time_anchors: Hostage captivity lasted overnight until morning
time_windows: Hostage event from night to next morning
Sale of wheat executed at dawn

inference_path.observation: Stanley Rees disappeared mysteriously from his hotel room leaving coat and hat behind
inference_path.correction: Rees was abducted and brought to Dredlinton House
inference_path.effect: Rees is a victim, not a voluntary runaway
required_evidence: Statement from hotel manager about Rees' disappearance
Testimony of Rees' valet about the noise and missing master

inference_path.observation: Phipps and Dredlinton are missing and unaccounted for
inference_path.correction: They are held captive in Dredlinton House
required_evidence: Servant Grant's testimony about their presence
Physical evidence of bindings and gags in the house

inference_path.observation: Wingate openly threatens the directors and controls the house
inference_path.correction: Wingate is the orchestrator of the kidnapping
inference_path.effect: Wingate is the mastermind behind the blackmail

inference_path.observation: A coded cable message reveals a secret shipment of wheat
inference_path.correction: The shipment will break the wheat corner if shares are sold
inference_path.effect: The motive for the kidnapping is to force sale of shares

inference_path.correction: They are held hostage and threatened with death
inference_path.effect: Their compliance is coerced by Wingate

Telephone orders to sell wheat at reduced price

inference_path.observation: Lord Dredlinton dies suddenly during captivity
inference_path.correction: Death caused by exhaustion and heart disease exacerbated by stress
inference_path.effect: The hostage situation has fatal consequences
required_evidence: Doctor's report certifying cause of death
Observation of Dredlinton's condition during captivity

inference_path.observation: After sale orders, the market collapses and wheat prices fall
inference_path.correction: The blackmail achieves its goal of breaking the corner
required_evidence: Telephone confirmation of sales to Harrison

discriminating_test.design: Wingate arranges for the three directors to be confined together in a locked room within Dredlinton House, with all access controlled by his trusted servants. The test is to verify that no one outside this circle could have entered or left unnoticed during the relevant time window, by checking servants' testimonies, access records, and the physical security of the house.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: This test reveals that the disappearance and captivity could only have been orchestrated by someone with full control of the house and servants, eliminating external suspects.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: No evidence of unauthorized entry or exit during the captivity period is found, confirming the closed circle of suspects.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given access to all key characters, their motives, and movements. The coded cable message is presented and can be decoded by attentive readers. The presence of servants loyal to Wingate and the locked house are described in detail. The false assumption about Rees' voluntary disappearance is clearly contradicted by witness statements and the physical evidence of captivity. The final confession and unmasking are foreshadowed, allowing the reader to deduce the true mechanism.
